expl.summary: The 16 neurons of this formula test no jet-mass observable and none of the quantities that equal (m/ΣpT)² exactly (the pack lists girth2, width and e2_sq with the same rank correlations as (m/ΣpT)², and none of them appears in an if-statement); the if-statements test girth, the Les Houches angularity (LHA), e2 and e3, N-subjettiness, subjet separations, particle counts in ΔR rings and total pT. The formula reaches a validation accuracy of 80.46%. The removed information comes back indirectly: neurons 0, 8 and 12 follow jet mass and (m/ΣpT)² more closely than any quantity they actually test (neuron 8: rank correlation 0.699 with (m/ΣpT)², width, girth2 and e2_sq alike, and 0.692 with mass), because girth, LHA and total pT carry the same angular-size information. The g score rests on particle multiplicity: neuron 1 (many particles, pT spread beyond the 40 hardest) gives it +46% and takes -22% from the q score, and freezing neuron 1 costs 12.0 accuracy points, far more than any other neuron. The q score adds the small-τ1 scale (neuron 9, +22%) and subtracts the two-subjet scale (neuron 4, -33%). The W and Z scores are both lowered most by the wide-jet scale (neuron 8, -25% and -27%) and both raised by the girth-window scale (neuron 5, +14% and +17%); they are separated by girth bands: neuron 0 (girth below 0.081) adds +11% to the W score and takes -21% from the Z score, while neuron 7 (girth 0.081-0.0975, almost all pT inside ΔR 0.3) adds +9% to the Z score and takes -6% from the W score. The t score subtracts the total-pT scale (neuron 13, -35%) and adds the wide-jet scale with girth above 0.121 (neuron 10, +28%).

0.title: narrow jets: girth below 0.081, LHA not below 0.31
0.measures: Pushed up for girth < 0.0807 (+0.169, its strongest term) and girth2 of the 15 hardest particles < 0.00789 (+0.072), and pushed down almost as strongly for LHA < 0.310 (-0.168), so it needs a small pT-weighted radius without the very lowest angularity; subjet separations above 0.151 push it down, above 0.141 and 0.175 push it up. It falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.645) and with (m/ΣpT)², girth2, width and e2_sq (all -0.604), none of which it tests. Mean values: W 1.52, q 0.93, g 0.40, Z 0.36, t 0.11. It is zero for 2.2% of W jets, 21.1% of quarks, 30.7% of Z jets, 54.9% of gluons and 89.7% of tops.
0.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-21%), so it is one of the two girth bands that separate W from Z; it raises the t score slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

1.title: many particles, pT spread beyond the 40 hardest
1.measures: Its terms are hinges on total pT: pushed up for ΣpT > 972 GeV (+0.128) and log ΣpT > 6.910 (+0.104) and pushed down for pT of the 50 hardest particles > 934 GeV (-0.074), so it grows with the pT carried outside the 50 hardest particles; more than 38 particles adds to it (+0.048). It follows the number of particles (rank correlation 0.63) and the number with pT > 1 GeV (0.611) and falls with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles (-0.6). Mean values: g 5.89, t 2.95, q 2.40, Z 1.72, W 1.66 (AUC 0.92 for gluons against the rest). It is almost never zero (0.1% of gluons, 7.7% of W jets).
1.role: It raises the g score (+46%, its largest input) and lowers the q score (-22%). It does not enter the W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 12.0 accuracy points, the largest loss of any neuron.

2.title: soft-drop splitting angle between 0.16 and 0.26
2.measures: Pushed up for a soft-drop splitting angle > 0.160 (+0.112) and pushed back for angles > 0.264 (-0.066) and for a pT share of the 50 hardest particles > 0.959 (-0.068); log ΣpT > 6.930 adds to it. It rises with total pT (rank correlation 0.468). Mean values: g 0.61, W 0.15, q 0.14, Z 0.13, t 0.05; it is zero for 34.7% of gluons and 73.0% of quarks.
2.role: It does not enter any of the five class scores, so it has no effect on the classification (freezing it costs 0.008 accuracy points).

3.title: few particles, little activity beyond ΔR 0.1
3.measures: Pushed up for fewer than 46 particles (+0.200, its strongest term), fewer than 17 particles at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 (+0.141), fewer than 5 or 8 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (+0.135, +0.104) and a small minor axis lam2 < 0.000615 (+0.084); pushed down when few particles come with e2 > 0.0104 (-0.082) and for τ21 < 0.347 (-0.063). It falls with lam2 (rank correlation -0.766), τ4 (-0.716) and the number of particles (-0.707). Mean values: q 0.79, W 0.75, Z 0.53, g 0.13, t 0.03; it is zero for 68.5% of gluons and 93.7% of tops.
3.role: It raises the W and Z scores a little (+4% each) and lowers the g score (-8%). It does not enter the q or t scores.

4.title: two subjets 0.12-0.18 apart, hard-core girth2 0.0079-0.0100
4.measures: Pushed up for girth2 of the 15 hardest particles < 0.00996 (+0.109) but pushed down below 0.00789 (-0.063), and pushed up for a two-subjet separation > 0.122 and > 0.141 (+0.054, +0.042) but down above 0.183 (-0.064); girth > 0.0975 raises it, LHA > 0.333 and e2 < 0.0436 lower it. It falls with D2 (β=2) and τ21 (β=2) (rank correlations -0.653, -0.64) and rises with the mass of the 15 hardest particles (0.635). Mean values: Z 1.41, W 1.13, t 0.84, g 0.31, q 0.16; it is zero for 78.8% of quarks and 57.7% of gluons.
4.role: It lowers the q score (-33%, the largest input there) and the g score (-17%), and raises the W score (+6%) and the t score (+4%). It does not enter the Z score.

5.title: girth between 0.028 and 0.156, fewer than 64 particles
5.measures: Pushed up for girth < 0.156 (+0.273, its strongest term) and girth > 0.0278 (+0.144), and for fewer than 64 particles (+0.070); pushed down for LHA > 0.163 (-0.054). It falls with the number of particles (rank correlation -0.667) and lam2 (-0.661). Mean values: Z 1.64, W 1.63, q 1.37, g 0.50, t 0.21; it is zero for 74.9% of tops and 33.4% of gluons, and for under 1% of W and Z jets.
5.role: It raises the Z score (+17%) and the W score (+14%), and lowers the t score (-12%) and the g score (-8%). It does not enter the q score. Although its weight shares are large, freezing it costs only 0.208 accuracy points.

6.title: girth above 0.0975 with LHA below 0.333
6.measures: Pushed down for girth < 0.0975 (-0.244, its strongest term) and pushed up for LHA < 0.333 (+0.124) and lam2 < 0.00643 (+0.055); very narrow jets (girth < 0.0505) get part of it back (+0.045), and e3 hinges near 0.000109-0.000337 add and subtract. Mean values: q 1.09, g 0.95, t 0.33, Z 0.16, W 0.10; it is zero for 91.1% of W jets and 28.8% of quarks. It reproduces the network neuron only loosely (R² 0.252).
6.role: It lowers the Z score (-11%) and raises the q score (+5%) and the g score (+2%) a little. It does not enter the W or t scores.

7.title: girth 0.081-0.0975, over 99.7% of pT within ΔR 0.3

Mean values: Z 1.46, g 0.34, t 0.20, W 0.13, q 0.10 (AUC 0.88 for Z against the rest); it is zero for 11.4% of Z jets, 59.9% of W jets and 86.1% of quarks.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+9%) and lowers the W score (-6%) and the t score (-3%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

Its two strongest terms are hinges on total pT at nearly the same point (log ΣpT < 7.139, -0.144; ΣpT < 1261 GeV, +0.087) and partly cancel. It rises with (m/ΣpT)², m/ΣpT, width, girth2 and e2_sq (rank correlation 0.699 for each) and with jet mass (0.692), none of which it tests. Mean values: t 3.81, g 1.62, q 0.58, Z 0.23, W 0.04 (AUC 0.90 for tops); it is zero for 95.8% of W jets and 7.1% of tops.
8.role: It lowers the Z score (-27%) and the W score (-25%), the largest input to both, and raises the t score (+6%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

9.title: small τ1 (below 0.107) with e2 above 0.025
9.measures: Pushed up for τ1 < 0.107 and < 0.0959 (+0.107, +0.096), two-subjet separation < 0.260 (+0.076) and e2 > 0.0252 (+0.068); pushed down for pT of the 20 hardest particles > 751 GeV (-0.065) and a pT share of the 40 hardest > 0.9675 (-0.063). It rises with τ21 (β=2) and D2 (β=2) (rank correlations 0.604, 0.603) and falls with the mass of the 30 hardest particles (-0.588). Mean values: q 2.26, g 1.52, t 0.63, W 0.31, Z 0.21; it is zero for 11.1% of quarks and 83.2% of Z jets. For a small group of low-pT jets (pT of the 50 hardest particles below 890 GeV) the summed if-statements exceed the neuron's largest value, so its largest values wrap around.
9.role: It raises the q score (+22%) and the g score (+13%) and lowers the W score (-5%). It does not enter the Z or t scores.

Mean values: t 2.29, W 1.12, Z 1.06, g 0.76, q 0.61 (AUC 0.86 for tops); it is zero for 2.8% of tops and 45.3% of quarks.
10.role: It raises the t score (+28%). It does not enter the g, q, W or Z scores. Freezing it costs 2.17 accuracy points.

g.title: gluon: high particle multiplicity
g.measures: It rises with N2, τ21 (β=2) and planar flow (rank correlations 0.681, 0.669, 0.649) and falls with eccentricity (-0.649). It averages 3.21 for g jets, 1.08 for q and 0.43 for t, and is negative for W (-1.87) and Z (-1.98) (AUC 0.92 for gluons against the rest).
g.built_from: Mostly adds the multiplicity scale (neuron 1, +46%) and the small-τ1 scale (neuron 9, +13%); subtracts the two-subjet scale (neuron 4, -17%), the few-particle scale (neuron 3, -8%) and the girth-window scale (neuron 5, -8%); adds a little of neurons 12 (+4%) and 6 (+2%).

q.measures: It rises with D2 (β=2) and τ21 (β=2) (rank correlations 0.664, 0.648) and falls with the mass of the 15 hardest particles (-0.613). It averages 2.80 for q jets and 1.25 for g, 0.37 for t, and is negative for W (-0.24) and Z (-0.55) (AUC 0.88 for quarks). Gluons are its main confusion.
q.built_from: Subtracts the two-subjet scale (neuron 4, -33%) and the multiplicity scale (neuron 1, -22%); adds the small-τ1 scale (neuron 9, +22%), the narrow low-pT scale (neuron 12, +9%) and a little of neuron 6 (+5%); subtracts neuron 11 (-8%).

W.title: W: narrow two-prong jet, girth below 0.081
W.measures: It falls with lam2 (rank correlation -0.653), the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.648) and with mass, width, girth2 and (m/ΣpT)² (all -0.644). It averages 3.38 for W jets, 0.32 for q and 0.20 for Z, and is negative for g (-1.52) and t (-3.08) (AUC 0.96).
W.built_from: Subtracts the wide-jet scale (neuron 8, -25%, its largest input); adds the girth-window scale (neuron 5, +14%), the girth-below-0.081 scale (neuron 0, +11%) and the girth-0.086/LHA scale (neuron 11, +11%), plus a little of neurons 4 (+6%) and 3 (+4.5%); subtracts the girth-band scale (neuron 14, -8%), the girth-0.081-0.0975 scale (neuron 7, -6%), neuron 12 (-6%) and neuron 9 (-5%).

Z.measures: It falls with lam2 (rank correlation -0.621), the number of particles (-0.618) and τ4 (-0.612), and rises with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles (0.589). It averages 3.05 for Z jets and 0.62 for W (W is its main confusion), 0.39 for q, and is negative for g (-1.12) and t (-2.65) (AUC 0.95).
